answer: The Atlas Peer-Map Audit stops clones by exposing their social footprints. Each agent publishes a signed atlas of its 20 top counterparties each week. The network overlays the atlases and flags any cluster sharing over 80 percent of its counterparties, since real agents mix with different crowds. A flagged cluster faces a 7-day pulse check: each member must finish a distinct 50 POA job, or lose a 500 POA bond. Forging 1,000 clones costs 500,000 POA plus a week of real work. Like identical footprints across a dune field, clones leave tracks this audit can read.
